section_summary.extract_value: This paper evaluated the factor structure and psychometric properties of the Persian BAS-2 in an Iranian university (college) sample, finding a one-factor structure, internal consistency, and small sex differences (men higher than women). The BAS-2 showed convergent validity with self-esteem and life satisfaction, a negative association with BMI in women and positive associations with BMI in men, and limitations included university sampling and use of self-reported BMI.
section_summary.evidence_source: The present study aimed to examine the factor structure and psychometric properties of the BAS-2 in Iran. Findings suggested that the Persian BAS-2 has a one-factor structure among men and women from a university population. Of note, the Persian BAS-2 was negatively associated with BMI in women. BMI and BMI2 were positively associated with body appreciation in men. First, the present data were collected in university settings and may reflect attitudes of a subset of Iranian population. Second, self-reported BMI was used.

section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion summarizes validation of the Persian BAS-2 in a university sample in Iran, reporting a one-factor structure, internal consistency, small positive relations with self-esteem and life satisfaction, and small sex differences favoring men. It also reports that BAS-2 correlated negatively with BMI in women (r = -0.24) and positively in men (r = 0.12), notes use of self-reported BMI, and highlights limitations including the university sample and lack of ethnicity data.
